what_its_for: Codeine is a pain reliever used to treat mild to moderately severe pain. It is also found in some cough medicines to help reduce a dry, bothersome cough. It belongs to a group of medicines called opioids (narcotics).
how_to_take: Take codeine exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may help if it upsets your stomach. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you have a liquid form, use the measuring device that came with your medicine — never use a regular kitchen spoon, as you could take the wrong amount. Do not take more than prescribed or take it more often than directed. Never crush, break, or chew extended-release forms of this medicine.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your age, weight, and how much pain you have. Adults are usually prescribed 15 to 60 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Never take more than 360 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you to. For children, dosing is carefully calculated by weight — always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Do not adjust your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you are taking codeine on a regular schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store codeine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture — do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a secure location, out of reach of children and pets. Never share your codeine with anyone else — it is illegal and dangerous. If you have leftover codeine you no longer need, dispose of it safely. Many pharmacies offer drug take-back programs, or you can mix it with an undesirable substance like coffee grounds and seal it in a bag before throwing it in the trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking codeine — this combination can cause serious side effects including extreme drowsiness, slow breathing, and can even be life-threatening. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how codeine affects you, as it can cause dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or other pain medicines, without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Do not stop taking codeine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this may cause withdrawal symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: very slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; blue or grayish color around your lips, fingernails, or skin; severe dizziness or fainting; chest pain; seizures; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice: severe constipation that does not improve; nausea and vomiting that is getting worse; confusion or unusual thoughts or behaviors; or if you feel you need to take more medicine than prescribed to get the same effect (this may be a sign of dependence).
when_it_works: Codeine usually starts to relieve pain within 30 to 60 minutes after you take a dose. The pain-relieving effect typically lasts about 4 to 6 hours. If your pain is not being controlled well, contact your doctor — do not take extra doses on your own.
special_populations: CHILDREN: Codeine should NOT be used in children under 12 years old. It should also NOT be given to anyone under 18 years old after certain surgeries such as tonsil or adenoid removal. Some children process codeine much faster than normal, which can lead to dangerously high levels in their blood. ELDERLY PATIENTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of codeine, especially dizziness, drowsiness, and constipation. A lower dose is often recommended. PREGNANCY: Codeine should be avoided during pregnancy, especially near the time of delivery, as it can cause withdrawal symptoms and breathing problems in the newborn. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do not take codeine if you are breastfeeding. Codeine passes into breast milk and can cause serious harm or even death to a nursing baby. LIVER OR KIDNEY PROBLEMS: If you have liver or kidney disease, tell your doctor before taking codeine, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
